title: Multiple outbreaks of norovirus caused by persistent transmission in a hospitality setting in Victoria, Australia, 2023.
abstract: This report describes unusually persistent transmission of norovirus in a hospitality setting in Victoria, Australia. In September 2023, the Victorian State Government Department of Health was notified of six gastroenteritis outbreaks associated with events held at a single function venue. Genomically identical norovirus genogroup II (GII) was detected from cases in five of the outbreaks. No statistically significant association with illness was found for any food item. Information collected through staff interviews provided evidence of food handlers and wait staff continuing to work while infectious, likely resulting in sustained transmission through person-to-person routes as well as through potential contamination of the environment.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This report describes unusually persistent transmission of norovirus in a hospitality setting in Victoria, Australia. The study aimed to investigate the causes and patterns of multiple gastroenteritis outbreaks linked to a single function venue.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In September 2023, the Victorian State Government Department of Health was notified of six gastroenteritis outbreaks associated with events held at a single function venue. The study focused on cases linked to this venue and included staff interviews to trace transmission patterns.
analysis.methods: Genomic analysis was used to identify norovirus strains, and staff interviews were conducted to gather information on potential transmission routes and contamination sources.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that sustained transmission occurred through person-to-person contact and environmental contamination, highlighting the need for improved hygiene practices in hospitality settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides insights into the persistence of norovirus in environments where close human contact is common, which can inform public health strategies for outbreak prevention and control.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates multiple norovirus outbreaks in a hospitality setting in Victoria, Australia, in September 2023. It highlights the persistent transmission of norovirus genogroup II (GII) across five outbreaks, likely due to person-to-person contact and environmental contamination. The research underscores the importance of hygiene practices in preventing such outbreaks. The study is observational and based on staff interviews, which limits the strength of the evidence. The findings have implications for public health strategies in managing norovirus in high-contact environments.

title: Bile and capsid variation coregulate histo-blood group antigen recognition and serum neutralization potency in GII.12 human norovirus.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis, with young children and the elderly bearing the greatest disease burden. GII strains cause the majority of HuNoV outbreaks globally, with host susceptibility influenced by genetic polymorphisms that regulate mucosal expression of histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) binding ligands. HuNoV viral capsid (VP1) diversity in residues adjacent to the conserved HBGA binding pocket selectively stabilizes ligand interactions. Additionally, select HuNoV capsids demonstrate bile-influenced conformational plasticity, further enabling HBGA engagement. Combined, these factors have the potential to enhance the breadth of binding of HuNoV to HBGAs, driving population susceptibility. Here we characterized two GII.12 outbreak strains that co-circulated cotemporaneously and were divergent at five key VP1 sites. Mutational analysis demonstrated amino acids at VP1 positions 373 and 392 coregulate HBGA ligand binding. Serological analysis demonstrated minimal antigenic impact at these positions. Broader GII comparisons demonstrated variable impacts of bile. Bile improved GII.2 and GII.12 binding to HBGA, in contrast to GII.4, GII.3, and GII.6. Further, bile reduced surrogate neutralizing antibody potency for GII.2 and GII.12 but not GII.4 and GII.6 strains. Collectively, these studies suggest that HuNoV bile-dependence is not a general feature of GII norovirus, but instead can be genotype or strain specific. These data inform how select GII HuNoV strains can modulate capsid residues linked to host-ligand and immune recognition, providing potential mechanistic evidence for continual viral circulation. IMPORTANCE: Human norovirus-host interactions are complex, influenced by viral diversity, host-ligand expression profiles, and the gastrointestinal environment. Periodically, outbreaks of endemic human noroviruses, like GII.12, demonstrate genetic diversity between viral strains of a genotype. Exploring this, two GII.12 outbreak strains were used to model the effects of genetic changes on the viral capsid ligand and antibody binding. Residue changes between the two strains modulated affinity for histo-blood group antigens that could be compensated for by addition of bile. Although bile improved HBGA-binding, it reduced serum and monoclonal antibody neutralization potency to GII.12. These observations demonstrate the balanced impact of bile-mediated viral capsid conformational plasticity in ligand recognition and potential immune evasion for select GII genotypes. Bile had similar effects for GII.2 HuNoV, but did not impact GII.6 or GII.4 HuNoV HBGA-binding and serum-ligand blocking potency, indicating that GII HuNoV strains potentially utilize multiple mechanisms to ensure host breadth and antigenic diversity.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how genetic variation in the viral capsid of GII.12 human norovirus influences its ability to bind histo-blood group antigens (HBGAs) and how bile affects this interaction. The research highlights that specific amino acid changes in the VP1 region of the capsid coregulate HBGA binding, and that bile can modulate this binding in some strains. Serological analysis showed minimal antigenic impact at these positions, while broader comparisons revealed that bile enhances HBGA binding for GII.2 and GII.12 but reduces neutralizing antibody potency. These findings suggest that bile-mediated conformational changes in the capsid may enable immune evasion in certain GII genotypes, potentially contributing to the virus's continued circulation. The study provides insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying host susceptibility and immune evasion in GII.12 norovirus, which could inform future research on viral adaptation and surveillance.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis, with young children and the elderly bearing the greatest disease burden. GII strains cause the majority of HuNoV outbreaks globally, with host susceptibility influenced by genetic polymorphisms that regulate mucosal expression of histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) binding ligands.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: Here we characterized two GII.12 outbreak strains that co-circulated cotemporaneously and were divergent at five key VP1 sites. Residue changes between the two strains modulated affinity for histo-blood group antigens that could be compensated for by addition of bile. Exploring this, two GII.12 outbreak strains were used to model the effects of genetic changes on the viral capsid ligand and antibody binding.
elements_en.methods: Mutational analysis demonstrated amino acids at VP1 positions 373 and 392 coregulate HBGA ligand binding. Serological analysis demonstrated minimal antigenic impact at these positions. Broader GII comparisons demonstrated variable impacts of bile.
elements_en.main_results: Bile had similar effects for GII.2 HuNoV, but did not impact GII.6 or GII.4 HuNoV HBGA-binding and serum-ligand blocking potency.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: These observations demonstrate the balanced impact of bile-mediated viral capsid conformational plasticity in ligand recognition and potential immune evasion for select GII genotypes. Collectively, these studies suggest that HuNoV bile-dependence is not a general feature of GII norovirus, but instead can be genotype or strain specific.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These data inform how select GII HuNoV strains can modulate capsid residues linked to host-ligand and immune recognition, providing potential mechanistic evidence for continual viral circulation.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength for the study.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这里,我们表征了两种同时共循环的GII.12 暴发株,它们在五个关键VP1位点上存在差异。两种株之间的残基变化调节了对组蛋白-血型抗原的亲和力,这种亲和力可以通过添加胆汁得到补偿。通过研究这种现象,我们使用了两种GII.12 暴发株来模拟遗传变化对病毒衣壳配体和抗体结合的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 突变分析显示,VP1位点373和392的氨基酸共同调控HBGA配体结合。血清学分析显示这些位点的抗原性影响较小。更广泛的GII比较显示胆汁对不同株的影响存在差异。
elements_zh.main_results: 胆汁对GII.2 HuNoV具有类似的影响,但对GII.6或GII.4 HuNoV的HBGA结合和血清-配体阻断能力没有影响。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些观察结果表明,胆汁介导的病毒衣壳构象可塑性在配体识别和某些GII基因型的潜在免疫逃逸中具有平衡影响。这些研究结果表明,HuNoV对胆汁的依赖性并不是GII 诺如病毒的普遍特征,而是可能与基因型或株种特异性相关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些数据阐明了某些GII HuNoV株如何调节与HBGA配体和免疫识别相关的衣壳残基,为病毒持续传播提供了潜在的机制证据。

title_zh: 胆汁和衣壳变异共同调控组蛋白-血型抗原识别和血清中和能力在GII.12人类诺如病毒中
source_body_en: UNLABELLED: Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis, with young children and the elderly bearing the greatest disease burden. GII strains cause the majority of HuNoV outbreaks globally, with host susceptibility influenced by genetic polymorphisms that regulate mucosal expression of histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) binding ligands. HuNoV viral capsid (VP1) diversity in residues adjacent to the conserved HBGA binding pocket selectively stabilizes ligand interactions. Additionally, select HuNoV capsids demonstrate bile-influenced conformational plasticity, further enabling HBGA engagement. Combined, these factors have the potential to enhance the breadth of binding of HuNoV to HBGAs, driving population susceptibility. Here we characterized two GII.12 outbreak strains that co-circulated cotemporaneously and were divergent at five key VP1 sites. Mutational analysis demonstrated amino acids at VP1 positions 373 and 392 coregulate HBGA ligand binding. Serological analysis demonstrated minimal antigenic impact at these positions. Broader GII comparisons demonstrated variable impacts of bile. Bile improved GII.2 and GII.12 binding to HBGA, in contrast to GII.4, GII.3, and GII.6. Further, bile reduced surrogate neutralizing antibody potency for GII.2 and GII.12 but not GII.4 and GII.6 strains. Collectively, these studies suggest that HuNoV bile-dependence is not a general feature of GII norovirus, but instead can be genotype or strain specific. These data inform how select GII HuNoV strains can modulate capsid residues linked to host-ligand and immune recognition, providing potential mechanistic evidence for continual viral circulation. IMPORTANCE: Human norovirus-host interactions are complex, influenced by viral diversity, host-ligand expression profiles, and the gastrointestinal environment. Periodically, outbreaks of endemic human noroviruses, like GII.12, demonstrate genetic diversity between viral strains of a genotype. Exploring this, two GII.12 outbreak strains were used to model the effects of genetic changes on the viral capsid ligand and antibody binding. Residue changes between the two strains modulated affinity for histo-blood group antigens that could be compensated for by addition of bile. Although bile improved HBGA-binding, it reduced serum and monoclonal antibody neutralization potency to GII.12. These observations demonstrate the balanced impact of bile-mediated viral capsid conformational plasticity in ligand recognition and potential immune evasion for select GII genotypes. Bile had similar effects for GII.2 HuNoV, but did not impact GII.6 or GII.4 HuNoV HBGA-binding and serum-ligand blocking potency, indicating that GII HuNoV strains potentially utilize multiple mechanisms to ensure host breadth and antigenic diversity.
abstract_zh: 未标注:人类诺如病毒(HuNoV)是急性胃肠炎的主要病因,婴幼儿和老年人承担着最大的疾病负担。全球范围内,GII型株导致了大多数HuNoV感染,其对急性胃肠炎的易感性受到调控黏膜表达组蛋白-血型抗原(HBGA)结合配体的遗传多态性的影响。HuNoV病毒衣壳(VP1)在保守的HBGA结合口袋附近的残基多样性选择性地稳定了配体相互作用。此外,某些HuNoV衣壳表现出胆汁影响的构象可塑性,进一步促进HBGA结合。综上所述,这些因素可能增强HuNoV对HBGA的结合范围,从而推动人群易感性。在这里,我们表征了两种同时共循环的GII.12 暴发株,它们在五个关键VP1位点上存在差异。突变分析显示,VP1位点373和392的氨基酸共同调控HBGA配体结合。血清学分析显示这些位点的抗原性影响较小。更广泛的GII比较显示胆汁对不同株的影响存在差异。胆汁增强了GII.2和GII.12对HBGA的结合,但对GII.4、GII.3和GII.6则没有这种效果。此外,胆汁降低了GII.2和GII.12的替代中和抗体效力,但对GII.4和GII.6株则没有影响。这些研究结果表明,HuNoV对胆汁的依赖性并不是GII 诺如病毒的普遍特征,而是可能与基因型或株种特异性相关。这些数据阐明了某些GII HuNoV株如何调节与HBGA配体和免疫识别相关的衣壳残基,为病毒持续传播提供了潜在的机制证据。重要性:人类诺如病毒与宿主的相互作用是复杂的,受到病毒多样性、宿主配体表达谱以及胃肠道环境的影响。有时,流行性人类诺如病毒,如GII.12,其病毒株之间会表现出基因型内的遗传多样性。通过研究这种现象,我们使用了两种GII.12 暴发株来模拟遗传变化对病毒衣壳配体和抗体结合的影响。两种株之间的残基变化调节了对组蛋白-血型抗原的亲和力,这种亲和力可以通过添加胆汁得到补偿。尽管胆汁增强了HBGA结合,但它却降低了对GII.12株的血清和单克隆抗体中和能力。这些观察结果表明,胆汁介导的病毒衣壳构象可塑性在配体识别和某些GII基因型的潜在免疫逃逸中具有平衡影响。对于GII.2 HuNoV,胆汁具有类似的效果,但对GII.6或GII.4 HuNoV的HBGA结合和血清-配体阻断能力没有影响,这表明GII HuNoV株可能利用多种机制确保对HBGA的广泛结合和抗原多样性。

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and multi-pathogen etiology of a norovirus GII-associated diarrheal outbreak in Bihar: a geostatistical analysis of localized spatial autocorrelation
abstract: Diarrheal disease outbreaks remain a persistent public health challenge in Bihar, India, often driven by complex environmental and socio-spatial determinants. While traditional epidemiological methods describe disease burden, they frequently underestimate the underlying spatial structure of transmission. This study investigates the etiology and spatiotemporal dynamics of an acute diarrheal outbreak in the Jehanabad district, utilizing geostatistical frameworks to objectively discretize high-risk transmission foci. A rapid outbreak investigation was conducted in the West Kako region, Jehanabad, Bihar following a surge in acute gastroenteritis cases in July 2025. Mixed-methods approach integrating active case finding, molecular diagnostics for enteric pathogens, and environmental water quality assessment was employed. To evaluate spatial dependency Global Moran’s I statistics to case coordinates was applied. Subsequently, local spatial autocorrelation was assessed using the Getis-Ord Gi statistic with Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) to identify statistically significant hot spots ( p < 0.05) of disease intensity within marginalized Mahadalit tolas. A total of 237 cases were identified, with the highest incidence among individuals aged < 20 years (55.2%). Environmental investigations identified microbiological contamination in household-stored drinking water and a household well, whereas no contamination was detected in the sampled PHED water supply source. Together with the observed spatial clustering of cases, these findings suggest localized environmental exposure potentially associated with point-of-use water contamination. Microbiological analysis revealed a multi-pathogen etiology, with Norovirus GII identified in 22.7% of stool samples ( n = 22) and Hepatitis A virus (HAV) detected in 5.6% of blood samples ( n = 18). Additionally, Escherichia coli was detected in 100% of the stool sample ( n = 16), which were not further screened for isolation of any specific strain. They were probably normal gut flora. However, possibility of presence of other common strains of E. coli causing diarrhoea in humans may not be completely ruled out. The geostatistical analysis confirmed significant global spatial clustering (Moran’s I = 0.1161, z = 3.64, p < 0.001). Localized hot spot analysis (Getis-Ord Gi*) identified high-intensity clusters (99% confidence, Bin + 3) specifically within Paswan and Manjhi Tolas. This study documents one of the first reports of Norovirus GII detection among patients investigated during an acute diarrhoeal disease outbreak in rural Bihar, highlighting a potentially evolving etiological profile. The application of localized spatial autocorrelation successfully transformed aggregate surveillance data into precise, statistically robust of disease clustering, supporting hypothesis of environmental exposure and subsequent person to person transmission rather than single confirmed outbreak source. By establishing a replicable geostatistical template for the objective discretization of disease clusters, this research demonstrates that integrating advanced spatial statistics into routine outbreak investigations enhances the precision of public health interventions in resource-constrained settings.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: Diarrheal disease outbreaks remain a persistent public health challenge in Bihar, India, often driven by complex environmental and socio-spatial determinants.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: A rapid outbreak investigation was conducted in the West Kako region, Jehanabad, Bihar following a surge in acute gastroenteritis cases in July 2025. A total of 237 cases were identified, with the highest incidence among individuals aged < 20 years (55.2%).
elements_en.methods: Mixed-methods approach integrating active case finding, molecular diagnostics for enteric pathogens, and environmental water quality assessment was employed. Subsequently, local spatial autocorrelation was assessed using the Getis-Ord Gi statistic with Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) to identify statistically significant hot spots ( p < 0.05) of disease intensity within marginalized Mahadalit tolas.
elements_en.main_results: Environmental investigations identified microbiological contamination in household-stored drinking water and a household well, whereas no contamination was detected in the sampled PHED water supply source. Microbiological analysis revealed a multi-pathogen etiology, with Norovirus GII identified in 22.7% of stool samples ( n = 22) and Hepatitis A virus (HAV) detected in 5.6% of blood samples ( n = 18). Additionally, Escherichia coli was detected in 100% of the stool sample ( n = 16), which were not further screened for isolation of any specific strain.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: Together with the observed spatial clustering of cases, these findings suggest localized environmental exposure potentially associated with point-of-use water contamination. This study documents one of the first reports of Norovirus GII detection among patients investigated during an acute diarrhoeal disease outbreak in rural Bihar, highlighting a potentially evolving etiological profile.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The application of localized spatial autocorrelation successfully transformed aggregate surveillance data into precise, statistically robust of disease clustering, supporting hypothesis of environmental exposure and subsequent person to person transmission rather than single confirmed outbreak source.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The geostatistical analysis confirmed significant global spatial clustering (Moran’s I = 0.1161, z = 3.64, p < 0.001). Localized hot spot analysis (Getis-Ord Gi*) identified high-intensity clusters (99% confidence, Bin + 3) specifically within Paswan and Manjhi Tolas.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 腹泻性疾病暴发仍然是印度比哈尔邦持续存在的公共卫生挑战,通常由复杂的环境和社会空间决定因素驱动。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在2025年7月比哈尔邦Jehanabad的West Kako地区发生急性胃肠炎病例激增后,迅速开展了暴发调查。总共识别出237例病例,其中<20岁个体的发病率最高(55.2%)。
elements_zh.methods: 采用混合方法,结合主动病例发现、肠道病原体分子诊断和环境水质评估。随后,使用Getis-Ord Gi统计量结合反距离权重(Inverse Distance Weighting,IDW)方法评估局部空间自相关性,以识别在边缘化的Mahadalit社区中具有统计学显著性(p < 0.05)的疾病强度热点。
elements_zh.main_results: Environmental investigations identified microbiological contamination in household-stored drinking water and a household well, whereas no contamination was detected in the sampled PHED water supply source. Microbiological analysis revealed a multi-pathogen etiology, with Norovirus GII identified in 22.7% of stool samples ( n = 22) and Hepatitis A virus (HAV) detected in 5.6% of blood samples ( n = 18). Additionally, Escherichia coli was detected in 100% of the stool sample ( n = 16), which were not further screened for isolation of any specific strain.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现与观察到的病例空间聚集现象相结合,表明可能与使用点水源污染相关的局部环境暴露。本研究记录了在比哈尔邦农村地区急性腹泻疾病暴发调查中检测到诺如病毒 GII的首批报告之一,突显了可能正在演变的病因谱。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 通过应用局部空间自相关,成功将聚合的监测数据转化为精确且统计学稳健的疾病聚集信息,支持了环境暴露和随后的人与人传播传播的假设,而非单一确认的暴发来源。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 地理统计分析证实了显著的全局空间聚集(Moran’s I = 0.1161,z = 3.64,p < 0.001)。局部热点分析(Getis-Ord Gi*)在Paswan和Manjhi社区中识别出高强度聚集区域(99%置信度,Bin + 3)。

title_zh: 比哈尔邦诺如病毒 GII相关腹泻的时空动态及多病原体病因:使用局部空间自相关分析的地理统计学研究
source_body_en: Diarrheal disease outbreaks remain a persistent public health challenge in Bihar, India, often driven by complex environmental and socio-spatial determinants. While traditional epidemiological methods describe disease burden, they frequently underestimate the underlying spatial structure of transmission. This study investigates the etiology and spatiotemporal dynamics of an acute diarrheal outbreak in the Jehanabad district, utilizing geostatistical frameworks to objectively discretize high-risk transmission foci. A rapid outbreak investigation was conducted in the West Kako region, Jehanabad, Bihar following a surge in acute gastroenteritis cases in July 2025. Mixed-methods approach integrating active case finding, molecular diagnostics for enteric pathogens, and environmental water quality assessment was employed. To evaluate spatial dependency Global Moran’s I statistics to case coordinates was applied. Subsequently, local spatial autocorrelation was assessed using the Getis-Ord Gi statistic with Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) to identify statistically significant hot spots ( p < 0.05) of disease intensity within marginalized Mahadalit tolas. A total of 237 cases were identified, with the highest incidence among individuals aged < 20 years (55.2%). Environmental investigations identified microbiological contamination in household-stored drinking water and a household well, whereas no contamination was detected in the sampled PHED water supply source. Together with the observed spatial clustering of cases, these findings suggest localized environmental exposure potentially associated with point-of-use water contamination. Microbiological analysis revealed a multi-pathogen etiology, with Norovirus GII identified in 22.7% of stool samples ( n = 22) and Hepatitis A virus (HAV) detected in 5.6% of blood samples ( n = 18). Additionally, Escherichia coli was detected in 100% of the stool sample ( n = 16), which were not further screened for isolation of any specific strain. They were probably normal gut flora. However, possibility of presence of other common strains of E. coli causing diarrhoea in humans may not be completely ruled out. The geostatistical analysis confirmed significant global spatial clustering (Moran’s I = 0.1161, z = 3.64, p < 0.001). Localized hot spot analysis (Getis-Ord Gi*) identified high-intensity clusters (99% confidence, Bin + 3) specifically within Paswan and Manjhi Tolas. This study documents one of the first reports of Norovirus GII detection among patients investigated during an acute diarrhoeal disease outbreak in rural Bihar, highlighting a potentially evolving etiological profile. The application of localized spatial autocorrelation successfully transformed aggregate surveillance data into precise, statistically robust of disease clustering, supporting hypothesis of environmental exposure and subsequent person to person transmission rather than single confirmed outbreak source. By establishing a replicable geostatistical template for the objective discretization of disease clusters, this research demonstrates that integrating advanced spatial statistics into routine outbreak investigations enhances the precision of public health interventions in resource-constrained settings.

title: Successful Nonsurgical Management of Norovirus-Triggered Necrotizing Enterocolitis in a Preterm Infant: What Is the Role of Immunomodulation?
abstract: Norovirus infection has been increasingly recognized as a potential trigger of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) in preterm neonates. Although previous reports have described severe cases associated with intestinal pneumatosis, bowel ischemia, and the need for surgical intervention, the clinical spectrum of Norovirus-related intestinal disease remains poorly defined. We report the case of a 29-week gestational age preterm infant who developed abdominal distension on the 35th day of life. Stool reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction confirmed Norovirus infection. Abdominal radiographs showed progressive development of intestinal pneumatosis, leading to the confirmed diagnosis of a stage IIA NEC. Abdominal pneumatosis resolved completely within five days, without evidence of perforation or clinical deterioration. The infant received only supportive therapy and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). This case highlighted the heterogeneous clinical spectrum of Norovirus-associated intestinal involvement in preterm infants and the possible protective and immunomodulatory role of the IVIG.

analysis.study_design_and_population: We report the case of a 29-week gestational age preterm infant who developed abdominal distension on the 35th day of life.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a preterm infant with Norovirus infection who developed stage IIA necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) but was successfully managed with supportive therapy and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the case report and the absence of comparative data.

title: Norovirus in hospitalized children with acute diarrhea after rotavirus vaccine introduction in Recife
abstract: Objective: To determine the frequency of norovirus and its genogroups in fecal samples of children under two years of age, hospitalized for acute diarrhea in northeastern Brazil. Methods: A cross-sectional, prospective study between February 2007 and April 2010. Acute diarrhea was defined as the presence of three or more stools of decreased consistency or the presence of at least one stool with visibly present blood within a 24-hour period, lasting up to 14 days. Stool samples were analyzed using RT-PCR. Results: A total of 103 children were studied. Norovirus was identified in 30.1% of the children, with genogroup GII identified in 100% of the positive samples. Vomiting was present in 74.2% of children with norovirus-positive fecal samples, representing a statistically significant association. Conclusion: Norovirus was identified as a major enteric pathogen, detected in one-third of hospitalized children with acute diarrhea. The significant association with vomiting reinforces its distinct clinical role in pediatric gastroenteritis. These findings underscore the need for continued surveillance and further research to understand the evolving epidemiology of viral gastroenteritis in the post-rotavirus vaccine period in Brazil.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the frequency of norovirus and its genogroups in children hospitalized with acute diarrhea following the introduction of the rotavirus vaccine in northeastern Brazil.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional, prospective study was conducted between February 2007 and April 2010, involving 103 children under two years of age hospitalized for acute diarrhea.
analysis.methods: Stool samples were collected and analyzed using RT-PCR to detect norovirus and determine its genogroups.
analysis.main_results: Norovirus was identified in 30.1% of the children, with all positive samples belonging to genogroup GII. Vomiting was present in 74.2% of children with norovirus-positive fecal samples, showing a statistically significant association.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight norovirus as a significant cause of acute diarrhea in young children, with a strong association between norovirus infection and vomiting.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results emphasize the importance of continued surveillance for norovirus in the post-rotavirus vaccine era and suggest the need for targeted research on its epidemiology and clinical impact in Brazil.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and the potential for unmeasured confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the direct detection of norovirus using RT-PCR and the clear association with vomiting.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the frequency of norovirus and its genogroups in fecal samples of children under two years of age hospitalized for acute diarrhea in northeastern Brazil following the introduction of the rotavirus vaccine. Using RT-PCR, norovirus was detected in 30.1% of the 103 children studied, with all positive samples belonging to genogroup GII. Vomiting was significantly associated with norovirus infection, occurring in 74.2% of cases. The study concludes that norovirus is a major enteric pathogen in this population, reinforcing its distinct clinical role in pediatric gastroenteritis. These findings underscore the need for ongoing surveillance and further research to understand the evolving epidemiology of viral gastroenteritis in the post-rotavirus vaccine period in Brazil. The study's cross-sectional design and reliance on RT-PCR provide strong evidence, though limitations include potential confounding factors.

analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight norovirus as a significant cause of acute diarrhea in young children, with a strong association between norovirus infection and vomiting.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results emphasize the importance of continued surveillance for norovirus in the post-rotavirus vaccine era and suggest the need for targeted research on its epidemiology and clinical impact in Brazil.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and the potential for unmeasured confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the direct detection of norovirus using RT-PCR and the clear association with vomiting.

title_zh: 诺如病毒在巴西东北部里约热内卢市引入轮状病毒疫苗后住院儿童急性腹泻中的流行情况
source_body_en: Objective: To determine the frequency of norovirus and its genogroups in fecal samples of children under two years of age, hospitalized for acute diarrhea in northeastern Brazil. Methods: A cross-sectional, prospective study between February 2007 and April 2010. Acute diarrhea was defined as the presence of three or more stools of decreased consistency or the presence of at least one stool with visibly present blood within a 24-hour period, lasting up to 14 days. Stool samples were analyzed using RT-PCR. Results: A total of 103 children were studied. Norovirus was identified in 30.1% of the children, with genogroup GII identified in 100% of the positive samples. Vomiting was present in 74.2% of children with norovirus-positive fecal samples, representing a statistically significant association. Conclusion: Norovirus was identified as a major enteric pathogen, detected in one-third of hospitalized children with acute diarrhea. The significant association with vomiting reinforces its distinct clinical role in pediatric gastroenteritis. These findings underscore the need for continued surveillance and further research to understand the evolving epidemiology of viral gastroenteritis in the post-rotavirus vaccine period in Brazil.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估在巴西东北部引入轮状病毒疫苗后,住院儿童急性腹泻中诺如病毒及其基因组群的流行情况。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 2007年2月至2010年4月期间,在巴西东北部进行了一项横断面前瞻性研究,涉及103名2岁以下因急性腹泻住院的儿童。
analysis_zh.methods: 收集并分析粪便样本,使用RT-PCR检测诺如病毒并确定其基因组群。
analysis_zh.main_results: 诺如病毒在30.1%的儿童中被检测到,所有阳性样本均属于基因组群GII。在诺如病毒阳性粪便样本的儿童中,74.2%出现呕吐,显示出统计学显著关联。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果突显了诺如病毒作为2岁以下儿童急性腹泻的重要病因,其感染与呕吐之间存在显著关联。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了在轮状病毒疫苗引入后,继续进行监测监测诺如病毒的重要性,并提出了针对其流行病学及其临床影响的进一步研究需求。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受限于横断面设计以及可能存在的未测量的混杂因素,但由于使用RT-PCR直接检测诺如病毒并明确其与呕吐的关联,证据强度较高。

title: Development of rhesus macaque enteroids and enteroid-derived cell lines for enteric calicivirus infections.
abstract: Recoviruses (ReCV) serve as valuable surrogates for fastidious human noroviruses (HuNoV). Although HuNoVs can be propagated in small intestinal enteroids, this system has several limitations, including low replication efficiency and an inability to sustain continuous propagation for generating infectious virus stocks beyond certain strains, such as GII.3. In contrast, ReCVs can be efficiently propagated in conventional cell lines (e.g., LLC-MK2), which has significantly advanced understanding of their biological characteristics. As a result, ReCVs are widely used as HuNoV surrogates. However, a physiologically relevant ReCV propagation system that closely mimics HuNoV enteroid cultures has not yet been described. Here, we report the establishment of intestinal stem cell-derived rhesus macaque enteroid lines representing both the small intestine and colon, along with two enteroid-derived cell lines. We further characterize these systems and evaluate their susceptibility to infection with three diverse ReCV isolates. Both small intestine- and colon-derived enteroids, as well as their corresponding cell lines, supported robust ReCV infection. The enteroids contained all major intestinal cell types. The duodenum-derived cell line comprised enteroendocrine cells (chromogranin A) and absorptive enterocytes (villin), whereas the colon-derived cell line included enteroendocrine cells and goblet cells (MUC2). Importantly, both cell lines formed tight barriers (transepithelial electrical resistance [TEER] > 3,000 Ω·cm2), making them far superior to LLC-MK2 cells (TEER ~ 100 Ω·cm2) for studies of viral entry and pathogenesis. The rhesus enteroids and intestinal cell lines developed in this study will enable comparative studies of HuNoV and ReCV replication in a physiologically relevant system and may have direct applications for culturing HuNoVs.IMPORTANCEHuman intestinal stem cell-derived enteroids have enabled the propagation of human noroviruses; however, this system has several important limitations, including high cost, low replication efficiency, and (except for a recent report for GII.3 human norovirus) the inability to sustain continuous virus propagation for the generation of infectious virus stocks. As a result, research still relies on human norovirus-containing clinical samples as the primary virus source. Here, we developed host-specific rhesus macaque enteroid cultures and two enteroid-derived cell lines that support robust recovirus replication. Studying recovirus replication in rhesus enteroids may help overcome key limitations of the human norovirus enteroid cultures. Moreover, because both natural and experimental human norovirus infections have been described in rhesus macaques, the rhesus enteroids and enteroid-derived cell lines described in this study may be directly applicable to human norovirus cultivation.

Although HuNoVs can be propagated in small intestinal enteroids, this system has several limitations, including low replication efficiency and an inability to sustain continuous propagation for generating infectious virus stocks beyond certain strains, such as GII.3. In contrast, ReCVs can be efficiently propagated in conventional cell lines (e.g., LLC-MK2), which has significantly advanced understanding of their biological characteristics. As a result, ReCVs are widely used as HuNoV surrogates. However, a physiologically relevant ReCV propagation system that closely mimics HuNoV enteroid cultures has not yet been described. Here, we report the establishment of intestinal stem cell-derived rhesus macaque enteroid lines representing both the small intestine and colon, along with two enteroid-derived cell lines. We further characterize these systems and evaluate their susceptibility to infection with three diverse ReCV isolates. Both small intestine- and colon-derived enteroids, as well as their corresponding cell lines, supported robust ReCV infection. The enteroids contained all major intestinal cell types. The duodenum-derived cell line comprised enteroendocrine cells (chromogranin A) and absorptive enterocytes (villin), whereas the colon-derived cell line included enteroendocrine cells and goblet cells (MUC2). Importantly, both cell lines formed tight barriers (transepithelial electrical resistance [TEER] > 3,000 Ω·cm2), making them far superior to LLC-MK2 cells (TEER ~ 100 Ω·cm2) for studies of viral entry and pathogenesis. The rhesus enteroids and intestinal cell lines developed in this study will enable comparative studies of HuNoV and ReCV replication in a physiologically relevant system and may have direct applications for culturing HuNoVs.IMPORTANCEHuman intestinal stem cell-derived enteroids have enabled the propagation of human noroviruses; however, this system has several important limitations, including high cost, low replication efficiency, and (except for a recent report for GII.3 human norovirus) the inability to sustain continuous virus propagation for the generation of infectious virus stocks. As a result, research still relies on human norovirus-containing clinical samples as the primary virus source. Here, we developed host-specific rhesus macaque enteroid cultures and two enteroid-derived cell lines that support robust recovirus replication. Studying recovirus replication in rhesus enteroids may help overcome key limitations of the human norovirus enteroid cultures. Moreover, because both natural and experimental human norovirus infections have been described in rhesus macaques, the rhesus enteroids and enteroid-derived cell lines described in this study may be directly applicable to human norovirus cultivation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of current human norovirus (HuNoV) propagation systems by developing a physiologically relevant model using rhesus macaque enteroids and enteroid-derived cell lines. Recoviruses (ReCV) are used as surrogates for HuNoVs due to their easier propagation in conventional cell lines.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the development of intestinal stem cell-derived rhesus macaque enteroid lines from both the small intestine and colon, along with two enteroid-derived cell lines. These systems were evaluated for their susceptibility to infection with three diverse ReCV isolates.
analysis.methods: The researchers established rhesus macaque enteroid cultures and derived cell lines from them. They characterized these systems by assessing their cellular composition and evaluated their ability to support ReCV infection through measures such as transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER).
analysis.main_results: Both small intestine- and colon-derived enteroids, as well as their corresponding cell lines, supported robust ReCV infection. The enteroids contained all major intestinal cell types, and both cell lines formed tight barriers with TEER values exceeding 3,000 Ω·cm2, which is significantly higher than LLC-MK2 cells (TEER ~ 100 Ω·cm2).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that these rhesus enteroid systems provide a more physiologically relevant platform for studying ReCV replication compared to conventional cell lines. This development may help overcome key limitations of human norovirus enteroid cultures.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may enable comparative studies of HuNoV and ReCV replication in a more physiologically relevant system, potentially leading to improved methods for culturing HuNoVs and advancing research on norovirus infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study does not address the limitations of the human norovirus enteroid system directly, as it focuses on ReCV. However, the evidence is strong, as it demonstrates the successful establishment and characterization of rhesus enteroid models that support ReCV infection.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a physiologically relevant model for studying norovirus infections by creating rhesus macaque enteroid cultures and derived cell lines. The researchers established these systems and evaluated their susceptibility to infection with three ReCV isolates. Both enteroids and cell lines supported robust ReCV replication, with tight barriers formed by the cell lines, making them superior to conventional cell lines like LLC-MK2. The findings suggest that these models could help overcome limitations in human norovirus research and may have direct applications for culturing HuNoVs. The study provides a strong foundation for future research on norovirus biology and pathogenesis, though it does not directly address the limitations of human norovirus enteroid systems.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过开发一种生理相关的模型,解决当前人类诺如病毒(HuNoV)培养系统的局限性,该模型使用恒河猴肠道类器官和类器官衍生细胞系。Recoviruses(ReCV)由于其在常规细胞系中更容易培养,被用作HuNoV的替代物。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及从小肠和结肠中建立恒河猴肠道干细胞衍生的类器官系以及两种类器官衍生细胞系。这些系统被评估其对三种不同的ReCV分离株的感染敏感性。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员建立了恒河猴肠道类器官培养系统,并从中衍生出细胞系。他们通过评估细胞组成以及通过跨上皮电阻力(TEER)等指标来评估这些系统支持ReCV感染的能力。
elements_zh.main_results: 无论是小肠还是结肠来源的类器官,以及它们对应的细胞系,都支持了ReCV的强效感染。这些类器官包含了所有主要的肠道细胞类型,且两种细胞系均形成了紧密的屏障,其TEER值超过3,000 Ω·cm2,这显著高于LLC-MK2细胞(TEER ~ 100 Ω·cm2)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,这些恒河猴类器官系统相比常规细胞系提供了更生理相关的平台来研究ReCV的复制。这一发展可能有助于克服人类HuNoV类器官培养系统的关键局限性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于在更生理相关的系统中进行HuNoV和ReCV复制的比较研究,从而可能改进HuNoV的培养方法,并推动对诺如病毒感染的研究进展。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究没有直接解决人类HuNoV类器官系统的局限性,因为它专注于ReCV。然而,证据是强有力的,因为该研究成功建立了并表征了支持ReCV感染的恒河猴类器官模型。

abstract_zh: Recoviruses(ReCV)作为人类难培养诺如病毒(HuNoV)的有价值的替代物。尽管HuNoV可以在小肠类器官中进行培养,但该系统存在一些局限性,包括复制效率低以及无法持续培养以生成某些菌株(如GII.3)的感染性病毒颗粒。相比之下,ReCV可以在常规细胞系(如LLC-MK2)中高效培养,这显著促进了对其生物学特性的理解。因此,ReCV被广泛用作HuNoV的替代物。然而,目前尚未描述一种能与HuNoV肠道类器官培养密切相关的生理相关ReCV培养系统。在此,我们报告了建立代表小肠和结肠的恒河猴肠道干细胞衍生类器官系以及两种类器官衍生细胞系。我们进一步对这些系统进行了表征,并评估了它们对三种不同的ReCV分离株的感染敏感性。无论是小肠还是结肠来源的类器官,以及它们对应的细胞系,都支持了ReCV的强效感染。这些类器官包含了所有主要的肠道细胞类型。来自十二指肠的细胞系包含肠内分泌细胞(染色体颗粒A)和吸收性肠上皮细胞(绒毛蛋白),而来自结肠的细胞系则包含肠内分泌细胞和杯状细胞(MUC2)。重要的是,这两种细胞系均形成了紧密的屏障(跨上皮电阻力[TEER] > 3,000 Ω·cm2),使其在研究病毒入侵和诺如病毒方面远优于LLC-MK2细胞(TEER ~ 100 Ω·cm2)。本研究中开发的恒河猴类器官和肠道细胞系将有助于在生理相关的系统中进行HuNoV和ReCV复制的比较研究,并可能直接应用于HuNoV的培养。重要性:人类肠道干细胞衍生的类器官使人类诺如病毒(HuNoV)的培养成为可能;然而,该系统存在一些重要的局限性,包括成本高、复制效率低,以及(除最近报道的GII.3型HuNoV外)无法持续培养以生成感染性病毒颗粒。因此,研究仍然依赖于含有HuNoV的临床样本作为主要的病毒来源。在此,我们开发了针对ReCV的恒河猴肠道类器官培养系统以及两种类器官衍生细胞系,这些系统支持ReCV的强效复制。研究ReCV在恒河猴类器官中的复制可能有助于克服人类HuNoV类器官培养系统的关键局限性。此外,由于在恒河猴中已经描述了自然和实验性HuNoV感染,本研究中描述的恒河猴类器官和类器官衍生细胞系可能直接适用于HuNoV的培养。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过开发一种生理相关的模型,解决当前人类诺如病毒(HuNoV)培养系统的局限性,该模型使用恒河猴肠道类器官和类器官衍生细胞系。Recoviruses(ReCV)由于其在常规细胞系中更容易培养,被用作HuNoV的替代物。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及从小肠和结肠中建立恒河猴肠道干细胞衍生的类器官系以及两种类器官衍生细胞系。这些系统被评估其对三种不同的ReCV分离株的感染敏感性。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员建立了恒河猴肠道类器官培养系统,并从中衍生出细胞系。他们通过评估细胞组成以及通过跨上皮电阻力(TEER)等指标来评估这些系统支持ReCV感染的能力。
analysis_zh.main_results: 无论是小肠还是结肠来源的类器官,以及它们对应的细胞系,都支持了ReCV的强效感染。这些类器官包含了所有主要的肠道细胞类型,且两种细胞系均形成了紧密的屏障,其TEER值超过3,000 Ω·cm2,这显著高于LLC-MK2细胞(TEER ~ 100 Ω·cm2)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,这些恒河猴类器官系统相比常规细胞系提供了更生理相关的平台来研究ReCV的复制。这一发展可能有助于克服人类HuNoV类器官培养系统的关键局限性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于在更生理相关的系统中进行HuNoV和ReCV复制的比较研究,从而可能改进HuNoV的培养方法,并推动对诺如病毒感染的研究进展。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究没有直接解决人类HuNoV类器官系统的局限性,因为它专注于ReCV。然而,证据是强有力的,因为该研究成功建立了并表征了支持ReCV感染的恒河猴类器官模型。

title: Infections and Anti-N-Methyl-D-Aspartate Receptor Encephalitis in Children and Adolescents: A Scoping Review of Evidence Since the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Background/Objectives: Anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (anti-NMDAR) encephalitis is a common autoimmune encephalitis affecting children and adolescents. Its development has been associated with preceding or concomitant infections, particularly herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1). This scoping review characterized the association between infections and pediatric anti-NMDAR encephalitis, focusing on epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, treatment, and prognosis from January 2020 to August 2025. Methods: A scoping review was conducted according to the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) framework. PubMed was systematically searched using the terms NMDAR encephalitis AND infections AND children. Of 110 identified records, 13 studies met the predefined eligibility criteria. Results: HSV-1 was the most consistently reported infectious association, particularly in younger children. Clinical phenotype varied with age, with neurological manifestations predominating in younger children and psychiatric, behavioral, and cognitive symptoms becoming more prominent in adolescents. HSV-associated cases, particularly following extensive HSV-related brain injury, were associated with greater residual neurological morbidity and less favorable long-term outcomes. Other infectious agents, including SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus, influenza B, and norovirus, were reported less frequently, with limited evidence regarding their impact on disease course. Immunotherapeutic strategies were generally similar irrespective of preceding infection, although active or treatment-associated infections could influence treatment timing, sequencing, and infectious-risk considerations. Earlier immunotherapy was associated with more favorable neurological recovery. Conclusions: Infectious exposures, particularly HSV-1, appear to be associated with pediatric anti-NMDAR encephalitis, although causality cannot be established from the predominantly retrospective and case-based literature. Prospective, multicenter studies using standardized diagnostic and outcome measures are needed to clarify the infection–autoimmunity relationship and optimize early recognition and management.

abstract_zh: 背景/目标:抗N-甲基-D-天门冬氨酸受体(anti-NMDAR)脑炎是一种常见的自身免疫性脑炎,影响儿童和青少年。其发病与先前或同时发生的感染有关,尤其是单纯疱疹病毒1型(HSV-1)。本次范围综述旨在描述感染与儿科anti-NMDAR脑炎之间的关联,重点关注流行病学、发病机制、临床表现、治疗以及预后,时间范围为2020年1月至2025年8月。方法:根据Joanna Briggs研究所(JBI)框架进行了范围综述。使用术语NMDAR脑炎 AND 感染 AND 儿童在PubMed上进行了系统性检索。共识别出110条记录,其中13项研究符合预定义的纳入标准。结果:HSV-1是最常被报道的感染关联,尤其是在年幼的儿童中。临床表型随年龄变化,年幼儿童以神经系统表现为主,而青少年则以精神科、行为和认知症状更为突出。与HSV相关的病例,特别是伴随广泛HSV相关脑损伤的病例,与更严重的残留神经系统疾病和较差的长期预后相关。其他感染病原体,包括SARS-CoV-2、呼吸道合胞病毒、流感B型病毒和诺如病毒,报道较少,关于其对疾病进程影响的证据有限。免疫治疗策略通常与先前感染无关,尽管活动性或治疗相关感染可能影响治疗的时间、顺序和感染风险考虑。早期免疫治疗与更良好的神经系统恢复相关。结论:感染暴露,特别是HSV-1,似乎与儿科anti-NMDAR脑炎有关,但由于文献主要为回顾性和病例为基础,无法确立因果关系。需要进行前瞻性、多中心研究,使用标准化的诊断和预后评估方法,以明确感染与自身免疫之间的关系,并优化早期识别和管理。

title: Long-Term Survival of Human Enteric Virus Surrogates (Murine Norovirus, Rhesus Rotavirus, and Porcine Sapovirus) in Bottled Drinking Water.
abstract: Enteric viruses are major causes of food- and waterborne diseases. Due to the limited cultivability of many human enteric viruses, surrogate viruses are commonly used to model their environmental persistence. This study aimed to evaluate the not-well-understood long-term survival of murine norovirus (MNV), rhesus rotavirus (RRV), and porcine sapovirus (PoSaV), used here as cultivable surrogate viruses for human enteric viruses, in bottled drinking water. Bottled water artificially inoculated with each virus was stored at 4 °C, 25 °C, and 37 °C for up to 365 days, and viral infectivity was quantified using TCID50 and plaque assays, with the latter successfully applied for PoSaV quantification. The initial virus concentrations were 5.2 log10 TCID50/mL for MNV, 6.5 log10 PFU/mL for RRV, and 4.0 log10 PFU/mL for PoSaV. MNV and RRV remained infectious for at least one year at 4 °C, whereas PoSaV gradually declined and became undetectable by day 55. At 25 °C, the viral inactivation rate was accelerated: MNV became undetectable by day 160, RRV by day 320, and PoSaV by day 20. At 37 °C, a rapid inactivation rate was observed for all viruses, with MNV, RRV, and PoSaV becoming undetectable by days 20, 80, and 10, respectively. These results demonstrate the pronounced temperature-dependent survival of enteric viruses in bottled water. It is important to ensure the use of microbiologically clean source for bottled water as well as implement effective food and water safety management to minimise potential viral contamination. The long-term survival of MNV, RRV, and PoSaV in bottled drinking water was evaluated. The viral inactivation rate increased with temperature (25–37 °C). MNV and RRV remained infectious for at least 365 days at 4 °C. In our study, PoSaV demonstrated lower stability than both MNV and RRV. Enteric viruses are extremely persistent in bottled water at low temperatures.

title: A comparative analysis of ensemble and deep learning approaches for predicting viral gastroenteritis in paediatric patients
abstract: Viral gastroenteritis, primarily caused by rotavirus and adenovirus, remains a major contributor to paediatric morbidity and mortality worldwide. Early and accurate identification of viral etiology is essential for appropriate clinical management and antimicrobial stewardship. However, laboratory confirmation is often inaccessible in resource-limited settings. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model to predict rotavirus/adenovirus-positive acute gastroenteritis in children using observable clinical features, including symptoms, demographic factors, and vaccination status. A cross-sectional analysis was conducted on 320 paediatric patients with acute gastroenteritis, of whom 39.38% tested positive for rotavirus and/or adenovirus by rapid antigen testing. Twelve original clinical variables were expanded to 24 engineered features, incorporating symptom severity scores, interaction terms, and composite risk indicators. Class imbalance was managed using SMOTE. Eleven predictive models were evaluated, including eight traditional machine learning algorithms, two ensemble approaches, and one deep neural network. Performance was assessed using ROC-AUC, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score with five-fold stratified cross-validation. Seven predictors showed statistical significance ( p < 0.05), including stool type, dehydration, fever, vomiting, vaccination status, weakness, and vomiting frequency. The Extra Trees classifier achieved the best performance (ROC-AUC = 0.8795; accuracy = 84.38%), with strong cross-validation results (mean ROC-AUC = 0.8886 ± 0.0409). Engineered interaction features contributed substantially to model performance. The study developed a non-laboratory-based predictive model for rotavirus/adenovirus-positive gastroenteritis that, pending external validation, shows potential to support triage-level clinical decision-making and rational antibiotic use in resource-constrained settings.

title: Systematic functional, genomic, and safety evaluation of food-derived anti-human norovirus candidate Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001
abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001 is a yogurt-derived strain previously reported to bind GII.4 human norovirus (HuNoV) and inhibit viral replication in zebrafish larvae. Here, its in vitro probiotic properties and preliminary safety were evaluated together with whole-genome analysis. The 2.87-Mb genome (46.67% GC; 2757 coding sequences) shared 97.66% average nucleotide identity with L. rhamnosus GG ATCC 53103. L. rhamnosus YQ001 showed acid and bile tolerance, retaining approximately 30% survival after 3 h at pH 2.0 and over 40% after 4 h in 0.2% bile salts. During sequential simulated gastrointestinal digestion, L. rhamnosus YQ001 retained 35.98% survival after the gastric phase and 45.06% after the intestinal phase. L. rhamnosus YQ001 showed over 90% auto-aggregation at 24 h, while its cell-free supernatant exhibited DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging activities of 85.17% and 76.35%, respectively. Antibacterial activity detected by agar diffusion was abolished after pH neutralization, indicating that the observed inhibition was largely pH-dependent under the tested conditions. L. rhamnosus YQ001 was non-hemolytic and negative for gelatinase and nitroreductase activities. Overall, the phenotypic and genomic findings support the probiotic potential of L. rhamnosus YQ001, while further strain-specific functional and safety evaluation is warranted.

title_zh: 从食品中分离的抗人类诺如病毒候选菌株乳酸乳球菌YZQ001的系统功能、基因组和安全性评估
source_body_en: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001 is a yogurt-derived strain previously reported to bind GII.4 human norovirus (HuNoV) and inhibit viral replication in zebrafish larvae. Here, its in vitro probiotic properties and preliminary safety were evaluated together with whole-genome analysis. The 2.87-Mb genome (46.67% GC; 2757 coding sequences) shared 97.66% average nucleotide identity with L. rhamnosus GG ATCC 53103. L. rhamnosus YQ001 showed acid and bile tolerance, retaining approximately 30% survival after 3 h at pH 2.0 and over 40% after 4 h in 0.2% bile salts. During sequential simulated gastrointestinal digestion, L. rhamnosus YQ001 retained 35.98% survival after the gastric phase and 45.06% after the intestinal phase. L. rhamnosus YQ001 showed over 90% auto-aggregation at 24 h, while its cell-free supernatant exhibited DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging activities of 85.17% and 76.35%, respectively. Antibacterial activity detected by agar diffusion was abolished after pH neutralization, indicating that the observed inhibition was largely pH-dependent under the tested conditions. L. rhamnosus YQ001 was non-hemolytic and negative for gelatinase and nitroreductase activities. Overall, the phenotypic and genomic findings support the probiotic potential of L. rhamnosus YQ001, while further strain-specific functional and safety evaluation is warranted.
abstract_zh: 乳酸乳球菌YZQ001是一种从酸奶中分离的菌株,此前报道可结合GII.4人类诺如病毒(HuNoV)并在斑马鱼幼鱼中抑制病毒复制。本研究对其体外益生菌特性及初步安全性进行了评估,并进行了全基因组分析。该菌株的全基因组为2.87 Mb(GC含量46.67%;包含2757个编码序列),与乳酸乳球菌GG ATCC 53103的平均核苷酸同源性为97.66%。乳酸乳球菌YZQ001表现出酸和胆盐耐受性,在pH 2.0条件下3小时后存活率约为30%,在0.2%胆盐中4小时后存活率超过40%。在连续模拟胃肠消化过程中,乳酸乳球菌YZQ001在胃部消化阶段后存活率为35.98%,在肠道消化阶段后存活率为45.06%。该菌株在24小时后表现出超过90%的自聚集能力,其无细胞培养上清液表现出85.17%的DPPH自由基清除能力和76.35%的ABTS自由基清除能力。通过琼脂扩散法检测到的抗菌活性在pH中和后被消除,表明在测试条件下观察到的抑制作用主要依赖于pH值。乳酸乳球菌YZQ001不溶血,且不表现出明胶酶和硝基还原酶活性。总体而言,表型和基因组研究结果支持乳酸乳球菌YZQ001作为益生菌的潜力,但需要进一步进行菌株特异性功能和安全性评估。
